reuse.why: Adds a shared isNonWorkingDay used everywhere and extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend for holidays, but the daily-skip rule is not put into any shared function, so each consumer writes its own skip loop.

duplication.why: The `skipWeekend && frequency === 'daily'` decision and a bespoke skip/lookahead loop appear separately in getNextDate, schedule-template createScheduleList, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and getDatesInRange restates getUpcomingDates' schedule-building and weekend-move skeleton.

placement.why: Day classification sits correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip rule itself lives in server handlers and the budget template rather than next to getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps; two release notes and a type field are the expected supporting edits.

maintainability.why: Four independently written variants of 'what day does this occurrence end up on' (with different lookahead heuristics: 7+holidays, 400 days, ±3/4+holidays) must be kept in step for any future weekend/holiday change.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (budget/schedule-template.ts) branch on daily frequency and call isNonWorkingDay themselves instead of a single shared weekend-resolution function; getNextDate does the same inline.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip rule is reshaped per site: a find over take=7+holidays in getNextDate, an isSkippedDay closure in schedule-template, an unbounded loop with a 400-day guard in getUpcomingDates, and a `continue` in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained a `holidays` parameter; the daily-frequency special case was kept out of it and is re-decided at four call sites (getNextDate, createScheduleList, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange).
